data.holdout: 2025-07-01 onward — not loaded or inspected until the verdict is written
data.market_hours_note: FX is closed from roughly Friday 22:00 UTC to Sunday 22:00 UTC. Those bars are absent, never filled: a filled weekend bar has zero return and zero range, which mean reversion rules read as signal and volatility rules read as calm. The engine also excludes the return across every closure and holds no position through one, so a handful of Sunday opens cannot dominate the statistics.
data.source: dukascopy tick data aggregated to bars, see data/manifest/

decision_rule.note: Fixed before any result was computed. Not adjustable. Run diagnose.py --null afterwards for the cross-sectional picture; that is exploratory here and must be labelled as such.

derived.note: Detection limit: the smallest TRUE annualised Sharpe this design could find with 80% power at alpha=0.05. A null result from this sweep says nothing about edges smaller than this.

hypothesis: Moving average crossovers — the single most widely sold technical rule — produce no risk-adjusted edge after realistic costs, and no detectable directional tilt across the family, once selection over the full parameter space is accounted for. This is the out-of-market replication of SW-0005: identical search space, identical protocol, different asset class. Crypto results to date come from a single market over a single period, so they are not independent evidence of anything general. FX has different participants, different microstructure and far lower costs. If the pattern found in crypto is a property of markets rather than of that one sample, it should appear here too.

planning.sd_source: Verified against the downloaded files: EURUSD 48,777 / GBPUSD 48,772 / USDJPY 48,775 bars. Symbols are aligned to the shortest, so n_observations = 48772. Dukascopy delivered 670 million ticks across the three pairs; 408 weekend gaps per pair match eight years of market closures, and 9-10 non-weekend gaps per pair are public holidays, recorded not filled.

protocol.cost_note: 1.5 bps round trip total, against 6.0 bps for the crypto sweeps. Major FX spreads are roughly 0.1-0.2 pips on EURUSD; this is a deliberately conservative retail figure. Lower costs mean a smaller true edge is needed to survive, so a null result here is stronger evidence than a null in crypto.
protocol.execution_model: signal from bar t close, held over bar t+1, no partial fills, position capped at 1x notional per side
protocol.method: Fixed rules, no in-sample parameter fitting. Every variant evaluated over the full period; in-sample/out-of-sample splitting is done by CSCV at scoring time.
protocol.survivorship_note: symbols fixed at the start of the period, no delisting selection

search_space.enumeration_note: 5 entry_threshold x 3 exit_rule x 3 holding_cap_bars x 7 lookback x 3 symbols = 945 fully enumerated variants. No variant is excluded after the fact. entry_threshold is the ratio of slow to fast EMA span: 2.0 means a 20/40 cross.

title: Moving average crossover on major FX pairs, hourly
